technologies.name: Basic Biotech
technologies.description: Everything that lives, grows or feeds a colony. Every Biotech level raises colony food output by 5% and underpins terraforming.

technologies.name: Hydroponics
technologies.description: Soil-free agriculture in nutrient solutions under artificial light. The first step toward feeding colonies far from home.

technologies.name: Bionics
technologies.description: Artificial organs and grafts that the body accepts as its own. Medicine improves, and so does knowledge of how bodies cope with alien worlds.

technologies.name: Genetics
technologies.description: Organisms designed rather than bred. Engineered microbes become the terraformer's first dependable tool.

technologies.name: Metagenics
technologies.description: Seed stocks of self-assembling proto-life that can colonize a lifeless world within a generation.

technologies.name: Climate Control
technologies.description: Orbital mirrors and atmospheric processors steer weather at planetary scale. Harvests stabilize, and terraformers stop fighting the sky.

technologies.name: Air Conversion
technologies.description: Planet-scale processors that rebalance an alien atmosphere one gas at a time. Marginal worlds become worth settling.

technologies.name: Biofiltration
technologies.description: Transporter-linked filters strip disease from anything that passes through them. Crowded colonies stop fearing plague.

technologies.name: Eco-Modification
technologies.description: Terraforming plans now anticipate how every change ripples through a biosphere. Projects finish faster and fail less often.

technologies.name: Xenobiology
technologies.description: Cataloguing thousands of alien biochemistries turns up solutions no home ecology ever tried. Bioengineers borrow them freely.

technologies.name: Silicobiology
technologies.description: Contact with silicon-based and energy-based beings completes the picture of what life can be. Few secrets of living matter remain.

technologies.name: Basic Computers
technologies.description: Information science, from data storage to artificial reasoning. Every Computers level raises empire research by 5% and sharpens intelligence work.

technologies.name: Microtape Storage
technologies.description: Dense magnetic microtape holds a library on a spool the size of a thumb. Ship computers finally carry the data their crews need.

technologies.name: Linguistics
technologies.description: Adaptive translation matrices let computers follow spoken requests and parse unfamiliar languages. They also lay the foundation for the universal translator.

technologies.name: Data Imaging
technologies.description: Scanners fine enough to capture the arrangement of every molecule in a sample. The groundwork for replication and pattern storage is laid.

technologies.name: Duotronics
technologies.description: Daystrom's breakthrough architecture outperforms every electronic computer before it. Fully automated starship systems become practical.

technologies.name: Crystal Memory
technologies.description: Data etched into crystal holds for centuries and loads instantly. Research databases and sensor logs grow by orders of magnitude.

technologies.name: Quadritronics
technologies.description: The successor to duotronics, so dense that engineers coined a new measure, the quad. Ship computers begin to anticipate their operators.

technologies.name: Isolinear Optics
technologies.description: Optical data chips, slotted by the hundred into every console. The standard of every modern computer core.

technologies.name: Circuit Distortion
technologies.description: Computer cores wrapped in their own subspace bubble, where signals are no longer bound by lightspeed. Calculations that took hours now finish in moments.

technologies.name: Ultraconduction
technologies.description: Circuitry that runs cooler the harder it works. Enormous computer cores now draw a fraction of their old power.

technologies.name: Positronics
technologies.description: The positronic brain, the architecture of true artificial minds. The line between tool and mind begins to blur.

technologies.name: Basic Construction
technologies.description: Engineering, materials science and industrial method. Every Construction level raises colony industry by 5% and yields sturdier hulls and stations.

technologies.name: Gamma Welding
technologies.description: High-energy welding that fuses hull plates without softening the metal around the seam. Spaceframes become lighter and more reliable.

technologies.name: Integrity Fields
technologies.description: Integrity fields carry loads no alloy could bear on its own. Larger ships and taller orbital structures become possible.

technologies.name: Epitaxy
technologies.description: Materials grown atom by atom, free of the flaws that weaken cast metal. The resulting composites reinforce everything from habitats to hulls.

technologies.name: Phase Transition
technologies.description: A bonding method that briefly shifts one part out of phase and lets it settle into another. Joints stop being the weak point of a design.

technologies.name: Warp Fields
technologies.description: Low-power warp fields replace brute-force integrity generators. Very large structures become cheaper to hold together.

technologies.name: Diffusion Bonding
technologies.description: A refinement of phase bonding that leaves no seam at all, only one continuous part. Complex assemblies come out stronger than their pieces.

technologies.name: Nuclear Epitaxy
technologies.description: Heavy, durable alloys built up nucleus by nucleus at industrial scale. Premium construction materials become plentiful.

technologies.name: Electron Bonding
technologies.description: A cold welding process that leaves no heat scar and no weak zone. Assembly lines speed up, and repairs are as strong as new work.

technologies.name: Quantum Epitaxy
technologies.description: Fabrication precise to the quantum level. If a material can exist, a factory can now make it.

technologies.name: Holographics
technologies.description: Hard-light tools and work crews that exist only as long as a job needs them. Industry adapts at the speed of a software update.

technologies.name: Basic Energy
technologies.description: Power generation, containment and field physics. Every Energy level raises colony energy output by 5% and strengthens starship shields.

technologies.name: Force Fields
technologies.description: Invisible barriers that can hold, push or seal off matter. The first deflectors and containment fields appear.

technologies.name: Subspace Physics
technologies.description: The physics of the layer beneath normal space. Faster-than-light sensors and communications follow.

technologies.name: Matter Conversion
technologies.description: Matter and energy exchanged directly, on demand. The theory behind replicators and transporters is in place.

technologies.name: Graviton Physics
technologies.description: Controlled graviton emission yields artificial gravity, tractor beams and inertial dampers. Crews no longer feel every burn of the engines.

technologies.name: Power Distribution
technologies.description: Plasma conduits that carry power across a city as easily as through a starship. Colony grids grow larger and more efficient.

technologies.name: Antimatter Fusion
technologies.description: Reactors that burn heavier forms of antimatter for a far richer yield. Power plants become smaller, safer and more productive.

technologies.name: Virtual Particles
technologies.description: Stand-ins for rare elements, conjured from the quantum vacuum when a process needs them. Advanced shield and reactor designs stop waiting on the mines.

technologies.name: Ultraconductors
technologies.description: The physics behind materials that strengthen the current they carry. Power grids and shield emitters grow more efficient.

technologies.name: Wave Analysis
technologies.description: Instruments that measure the probability waves behind every particle. Physicists begin to read the universe at its root.

technologies.name: Determinacy
technologies.description: The art of nudging quantum outcomes toward the one you want. Its limits are not yet known.

technologies.name: Basic Propulsion
technologies.description: Engines of every kind, from impulse thrusters to warp coils. Every two Propulsion levels extend fleet supply range by one sector, and new hulls fly faster.

technologies.name: Warp Drive
technologies.description: The first engine to break the light barrier, crude but revolutionary. The nearest stars are finally within reach.

technologies.name: Distortion
technologies.description: Coils that bend space itself rather than pushing against it. Trips between neighboring systems shrink from years to days.

technologies.name: Plasma Injection
technologies.description: A new plasma feed that drives warp coils harder and more precisely. Warp fields grow stronger and easier to shape.

technologies.name: Microdistortion
technologies.description: Miniature warp coils for probes, shuttles and precision station-keeping. Larger ships maneuver more nimbly as well.

technologies.name: Field Manipulation
technologies.description: Carefully timed coil firings make a warp field far larger than the power spent on it. Big ships reach high warp without ruinous power demands.

technologies.name: Field Geometry
technologies.description: Computer-optimized nacelle placement and hull lines. Every new design is shaped around its warp field.

technologies.name: Superconduction
technologies.description: Better magnetic bottles for antimatter let a warp core run hotter in safety. Engine output climbs across the fleet.

technologies.name: Field Compression
technologies.description: Tighter, sleeker warp fields that spend less energy on empty space. Ships go faster on the same fuel.

technologies.name: Charge Reversal
technologies.description: Onboard antimatter production from ordinary matter. Expensive, but fleets can operate far longer between refuelings.

technologies.name: Ultraconductivity
technologies.description: Coils that feed on the energy of the very field they generate. The summit of warp engineering.

technologies.name: Basic Weapons
technologies.description: Everything that makes a phaser hurt and a torpedo explode. Every Weapons level adds to the striking power of fleets, troops and invasions.

technologies.name: Beam Emitters
technologies.description: The phaser's ancestor: a directed-energy weapon strong and accurate enough for ship-to-ship combat.

technologies.name: Torpedo Hardening
technologies.description: Torpedo casings that punch through a deflector before they detonate. More of each blast reaches the hull.

technologies.name: Beam Hardening
technologies.description: Beam emitters tuned to pierce deflectors rather than splash across them. Shields shed far less of every shot.

technologies.name: Matter Packets
technologies.description: An improved warhead design that turns more of its antimatter into blast. Every torpedo hits harder.

technologies.name: Multifreq. Beams
technologies.description: Beams that shift frequency faster than a shield can adapt. Deflectors lose their tuning advantage.

technologies.name: Subspace Guidance
technologies.description: Self-guided torpedoes that track their targets through subspace. Fewer shots go wide.

technologies.name: Micropulsing
technologies.description: Pulse-modulated beams that hit shields harder than a steady stream of the same power.

technologies.name: Compression
technologies.description: Denser antimatter storage that packs far more yield into the same torpedo casing.

technologies.name: Quantum Shielding
technologies.description: Shaped warheads that focus a torpedo's full yield on its target. Nothing is wasted.

technologies.name: Ultra. Emitters
technologies.description: The finest beam emitters ever built. The ultimate directed-energy weapon technology.

technologies.name: Sociology 0
technologies.description: Civic development, foundation tier: the customs and institutions every starfaring society begins with. Not researched directly; it gates civic, security and morale buildings.

technologies.name: Sociology 1
technologies.description: Civic development, tier 1: a professional civil service and the first planetary councils. Unlocks civic buildings of this tier.

technologies.name: Sociology 2
technologies.description: Civic development, tier 2: organized labor, public order and early state security. Unlocks civic buildings of this tier.

technologies.name: Sociology 3
technologies.description: Civic development, tier 3: mass media, public entertainment and formal intelligence services. Unlocks civic buildings of this tier.

technologies.name: Sociology 4
technologies.description: Civic development, tier 4: interstellar institutions that bind distant colonies to the capital. Unlocks civic buildings of this tier.

technologies.name: Sociology 5
technologies.description: Civic development, tier 5: elite academies and national symbols that shape every citizen's outlook. Unlocks civic buildings of this tier.

technologies.name: Sociology 6
technologies.description: Civic development, tier 6: sophisticated governance able to weather strain and crisis. Unlocks civic buildings of this tier.

technologies.name: Sociology 7
technologies.description: Civic development, tier 7: a mature society at ease with many worlds and many peoples. Unlocks civic buildings of this tier.

technologies.name: Sociology 8
technologies.description: Civic development, tier 8: institutions that anticipate unrest before it forms. Unlocks civic buildings of this tier.

technologies.name: Sociology 9
technologies.description: Civic development, tier 9: a civilization confident in its identity across the stars. Unlocks civic buildings of this tier.

technologies.name: Sociology 10
technologies.description: Civic development, tier 10: the peak of social organization. Unlocks civic buildings of this tier.

ships.description: The Union's standoff bombardment ship, built around a deep torpedo magazine. Use it to open battles and break planetary defenses; keep it out of close-range brawls.
A heavier Keldon refit with a larger warhead load and stiffer shields. Still a first-strike platform, now a lethal one.
Cardassian settler ship carrying colonists, prefabricated habitats and soil processors. Unarmed and slow: escort it to an unclaimed system and it founds a colony.
The late-model Ranol, better protected and fitted with modern terraforming kits. Same mission, better odds of arriving.
The symbol of Cardassian military power, armored like a fortress and armed nearly as well. As a command ship it steadies the task force it leads.
The Galor refit adds heavy phaser banks and still more protection. Central Command reserves it for its most trusted guls.
A small frontier station built on site by a transport crew. It extends fleet supply range, watches the surrounding sectors and can fend off light raiders.
An upgraded frontier station with more guns, thicker shields and longer sensor reach. It can hold a sector against anything short of a determined assault.
A fast Cardassian patrol ship with guns out of proportion to its armor. Ideal for catching scouts, transports and colony ships that stray across the border.
Upgraded targeting and a wider weapons fit let this Netel raid weakly held systems as well as patrol.
A cheap, far-ranging Cardassian scout with good sensors and token weapons. Send it ahead to chart systems and spot enemy fleets.
A faster, sturdier Nerok with the best sensors in the Union fleet. Good for shadowing enemy fleets, not for fighting them.
A fortress station built around an existing outpost, with repair docks, deep supply stores and heavy batteries. It anchors a key sector and every fleet operating from it.
A late-model starbase that is, in practical terms, a fleet that cannot move. Attack it with everything or not at all.
Cardassian troop carrier for ground invasions, whose hull also becomes the core of new outposts and starbases. Unarmed; never send it in alone.
More troop berths, heavier armor and stronger shields for landings under fire.
A Cardassian line cruiser built to kill ships and installations. Its reinforced frame fights on after its shields collapse.
A Neterok rebuilt with current-generation weapons and hull plating: durable and hard-hitting.
A heavy assault cruiser for cracking fortified systems. Slow, short-ranged and very hard to kill.
The Telok refit crams in yet more firepower. Few ships short of a dreadnought want to trade blows with it.
A Nebula-class hull fitted with a large torpedo pod. Deadliest early in a fight, and well suited to softening up a planet before an invasion.
Extra launchers and improved torpedo guidance let this Nebula saturate a target before the enemy closes.
Federation colony transport carrying settlers and everything a new human world needs. Unarmed; escort it through contested space.
A modernized Edward with stronger shields and up-to-date terraforming equipment.
Starfleet's great multi-mission ship, at home on a survey or in a fleet action. Its command facilities coordinate every ship in its task force.
A service-life refit of the Galaxy class: more weapons, stronger shields and the same superb command suite.
The newest ship of the line from Utopia Planitia, pairing long phaser strips and quantum launchers with formidable shields. It also leads the fleet around it.
The Sovereign refit, Starfleet's most heavily armed and best-shielded ship. The last word in Federation design.
A small frontier station built on site by a transport crew. It extends fleet supply range, watches the surrounding sectors and can fend off light raiders.
An upgraded frontier station with more guns, thicker shields and longer sensor reach. It can hold a sector against anything short of a determined assault.
An old but trusted Starfleet escort, cheap to build and dependable on frontier patrol against raiders.
Bigger engines and upgraded arrays turn the Miranda into a quick-reaction escort.
A four-nacelle escort that is heavier and faster than it looks. Raiders expecting an easy kill regret it.
A new drive and shield-penetrating weapon refinements keep this veteran design competitive.
A compact, overpowered warship built for one purpose: combat. Fast, heavily armed and able to beat ships twice its size.
A small Starfleet research ship with long range and excellent sensors. Use it to explore; keep it away from fights.
A tougher Oberth with longer sensor reach and enough weapons to survive a bad first contact.
A fortress station built around an existing outpost, with repair docks, deep supply stores and heavy batteries. It anchors a key sector and every fleet operating from it.
A late-model starbase that is, in practical terms, a fleet that cannot move. Attack it with everything or not at all.
Starfleet troop and construction transport, used to invade worlds and to build outposts. Unarmed and dependent on escorts.
More capacity and heavier shields, so more troops or builders arrive intact.
A dedicated battleship spun off from the Galaxy design, with a third nacelle and a hull crammed with weapons. It can soak up damage that would gut a lighter ship.
The refit tri-nacelle battleship adds heavier guns while keeping pace with escorts.
A sturdy, well-armed Starfleet cruiser for long patrols in dangerous space. Often the first real warship a growing Federation fields.
The Ambassador refit mounts modern arrays and shields, a clear warning to aggressive neighbors.
A Ferengi torpedo boat that settles disputes at long range, before the competition can close. Badly outgunned up close.
Reinforced shields and a bigger magazine make the refit Ooron a formidable standoff and bombardment ship.
Ferengi colony transport that opens new worlds to settlement, and to business. Unarmed and clumsy; escort it.
Better shields and modern terraforming gear, so the new colony turns a profit sooner.
The Alliance flagship, a reward for DaiMons with deep pockets and the right friends. Heavy weapons persuade rivals to negotiate; heavy shields guarantee a way out.
Faster, tougher and carrying upgraded torpedoes: the most expensive and most persuasive ship in the Alliance.
A small frontier station built on site by a transport crew. It extends fleet supply range, watches the surrounding sectors and can fend off light raiders.
An upgraded frontier station with more guns, thicker shields and longer sensor reach. It can hold a sector against anything short of a determined assault.
A cheap, fast hit-and-run raider that makes raiding pay. Easily written off when a raid goes wrong.
Uprated engines let this Ngort run down the fastest freighters, and its guns enforce Alliance impound law.
A fast, well-protected Alliance raider that polices trade lanes and seizes suspect cargo. Surprisingly well armed.
Uprated guns and engines make this refit the quickest raider in the quadrant.
A small Ferengi scout that hunts for opportunities and watches competitors. Its reports steer where the Alliance invests.
A long-range Bronta with a bigger drive and better protection, for prospecting at the edge of Ferengi space.
A fortress station built around an existing outpost, with repair docks, deep supply stores and heavy batteries. It anchors a key sector and every fleet operating from it.
A late-model starbase that is, in practical terms, a fleet that cannot move. Attack it with everything or not at all.
Ferengi troop carrier for hostile takeovers of the planetary kind, and a crew ferry for outpost construction. Unarmed.
More troops, bigger engines and better shields: an improvement on every line of the ledger.
A Ferengi line cruiser that guards Alliance holdings. Would-be corporate raiders meet it first.
A long-overdue refit: heavy torpedoes, better shields, quicker engines.
A coveted Klingon command that opens every battle with a torrent of torpedoes. Nothing of its tonnage carries more firepower.
More torpedoes and more disruptors. Its first volley often decides the fight.
A Klingon colony ship that carries light guns beside its settlers. It can see off a raider, but not a warship.
A refit with modern terraforming kits and heavier guns; the Empire settles worlds the way it takes them.
The Klingon fleet's favorite command: a cruiser carrying more and heavier weapons than almost any rival. It leads the charge.
An even deadlier Vor'cha, tougher all round and with longer-reaching guns.
A small frontier station built on site by a transport crew. It extends fleet supply range, watches the surrounding sectors and can fend off light raiders.
An upgraded frontier station with more guns, thicker shields and longer sensor reach. It can hold a sector against anything short of a determined assault.
A fast Klingon hunter with heavy guns for its size, able to operate far from support.
The refit May'Duj adds armor, shields and a far heavier gun deck. Escorts are no longer a worry.
The Klingon fleet's scout and raider, cloaked and quick. It finds the enemy first and picks off their support ships.
The refit B'rel trades some patience for real teeth; it now hunts as well as watches.
A fortress station built around an existing outpost, with repair docks, deep supply stores and heavy batteries. It anchors a key sector and every fleet operating from it.
A late-model starbase that is, in practical terms, a fleet that cannot move. Attack it with everything or not at all.
A Klingon assault transport with light weapons, so the warriors aboard can shoot back on the way in. It still needs escorts.
Larger troop holds and stronger weapons and shields, so it lands more warriors.
Klingon crews love this veteran design, rebuilt with modern armor and disruptors. It still out-slugs most cruisers.
The refit K't'inga carries modern shields and disruptors. With an aggressive captain it wins fights it has no business winning.
Klingon shipwrights took the Bird of Prey's lines and built a battle cruiser around them. It is all weapons and wings.
The ultimate refit of the Bird of Prey battle cruiser, with more engine and more gun than any before it.
A Romulan torpedo ship built around the cloak: decloak, empty the launchers, exploit the confusion.
More launchers, more disruptors and improved warheads make its opening strike devastating.
Romulan colony ship carrying settlers and equipment for new worlds. Unarmed; protect it in contested space.
Stronger shields, nimbler handling and improved terraforming equipment.
The great warbird at the heart of every Romulan task force. Its volleys can erase an unprepared fleet.
The refit warbird is the strongest ship the Romulan Empire has ever launched. Few enemies can face one alone.
A small frontier station built on site by a transport crew. It extends fleet supply range, watches the surrounding sectors and can fend off light raiders.
An upgraded frontier station with more guns, thicker shields and longer sensor reach. It can hold a sector against anything short of a determined assault.
A stealthy Romulan hunter that intercepts trespassers and preys on supply lines.
Better weapons and shields and, above all, much stronger engines make it a relentless pursuer.
A long-range Romulan explorer with just enough firepower to bully transports. Anything bigger sends it running.
Stronger engines to outrun larger ships, and shields that hold longer when it cannot.
A fortress station built around an existing outpost, with repair docks, deep supply stores and heavy batteries. It anchors a key sector and every fleet operating from it.
A late-model starbase that is, in practical terms, a fleet that cannot move. Attack it with everything or not at all.
Romulan troop and construction transport for invasions and outpost work. Unarmed.
An uprated R'daran whose bigger reactor drives both faster engines and stronger shields.
A Romulan battle cruiser with top-grade shields and heavy weapons, able to meet any cruiser head-on.
One of the strongest Romulan warships, with massive engines that answer threats quickly.
A cloaked ambusher tasked with making sure intruders deep in Romulan space never report home.
A full weapons swap makes the refit R'derex the most dreaded ambusher in the fleet.
A fast, mid-sized raider flown by the Acamarian clans. Nimble and well armed for its size, it is the kind of ship that made the Gatherers notorious.
A small, agile Bajoran attack craft, built by a people who learned to fight a far larger enemy. Cheap to field and quick to strike.
A light Ktarian raider that relies on cunning rather than power. It favors quick strikes over sustained combat.
A cobbled-together Pakled hull stuffed with weapons found, traded or borrowed. It is stronger than it looks, and it looks strong.
A Sheliak patrol raider that enforces treaty boundaries with precision and little patience. Tougher than most minor-race craft.
A heavily armed Talarian warship with strong shields and a reinforced hull. Talarian commanders favor direct assaults.
A sturdy, well-armored Tamarian cruiser. Its crew speaks in metaphor; its weapons need no translation.
A balanced Trill cruiser built to defend Trill space. Its commanders may bring several lifetimes of experience to the bridge.
A Vulcan research cruiser, logically equipped for both science and self-defense. It carries more firepower than its peaceful mission suggests.
A fast Yridian courier and scout, built to carry information to whoever pays best.
A cybernetic vessel of overwhelming power that repairs itself and adapts to its attackers. No single fleet should expect to survive contact.
A sentient cloud of ionized gas that engulfs ships and tears at their shields. It cannot be reasoned with and is hard to disperse.
A massive Chodak warship, heavily shielded and armed, that treats any vessel in its path as a target.
A vast crystalline lifeform that strips ships and worlds of organic life. Its lattice shrugs off conventional fire.
An autonomous weapons drone that outlived its makers and still hunts anything it does not recognize.
A godlike presence watching over the Edo homeworld. Its power is effectively unlimited; the wise simply leave.
A living starship, alone and searching the void. It does not attack, but its immense bulk withstands almost any assault.
A warship of the vanished Husnock, still roaming the dark. Heavily shielded and quick to open fire.
A fixed weapons platform guarding a system from orbit. It cannot move, but it defends its world with steady fire.
A plague ship of Tarellian refugees, drifting from world to world. Shunned everywhere, it fights when cornered.
Earth's first true deep-space explorer, a warp-five pioneer with polarized hull plating in place of shields. Cheap, reliable and utterly outclassed by anything built a century later.
A spherical-hulled cruiser from the Federation's founding decades. Roomy and robust, it carried the flag to many first contacts and still makes a stout frontier patrol ship.

roster.source: Model in DS9 (Sisko's office); named in TNG

ships.description: A slow boomer freighter whose crews spend their whole lives aboard. It hauls troops and prefabricated structures without complaint, and without much protection.
The legendary five-year-mission starship: explorer, diplomat and warship in one saucer-and-nacelle silhouette. An early-game workhorse that can do a little of everything.
A near-total rebuild of the classic hull with new engines, stronger shields and a denser phaser fit. It stays useful well into the age of the Excelsior.

roster.source: Star Trek: The Motion Picture; films II-VI

ships.description: A Miranda derivative with an extra sensor and weapons pod bolted aft. Slower than its parent but a far better picket for a border sector.
A compact personnel transport with a turn of speed its bulk freighter cousins lack. Troops arrive sooner; they do not arrive any safer.
Once the great transwarp experiment, later the most numerous capital hull in Starfleet. Tough, long-legged and easy to refit, it anchors many a second-line squadron.

roster.source: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock; TNG, DS9, VOY

ships.description: A small civilian research ship with an outsized sensor suite. Fragile and unarmed in all but name, it sees far and should never be seen.
A Galaxy-derived cruiser that trades the great saucer for a lean secondary hull. A capable line ship that shares spare parts with half the fleet.
A four-nacelle cruiser built around a compact saucer. Its extra warp coils buy acceleration rather than top speed, which suits fleet screening duties.
A modular light cruiser whose mission pod swaps between labs, cargo and weapons. Jack of all trades, prized by frontier governors.
A single-nacelle frigate that is little more than a saucer with an engine. Fast and cheap; it dies fast and cheap too.
A three-nacelle heavy cruiser that borrows Galaxy-era components. Solid shields and a deep phaser grid make it a steady anchor for a battle line.
A frigate with twin weapons pods above and below the saucer. It punches above its size and is often assigned to convoy duty.

roster.source: TNG (USS Kyushu, 'The Best of Both Worlds II')

ships.description: A spherical-hulled medical and research ship. Its labs and sickbays make it a fine explorer; its weapons are an afterthought.
A compact escort built on Excelsior-era parts with a modern weapons pod. Quick to build and quick in a fight, it filled the gaps of a wartime fleet.
A warp-capable runabout with a swappable mission module. Short range, but cheap, sturdy and far better armed than a shuttle has any right to be.
A small planetary survey ship packed with sensors. Its crew is tiny and its reach is long; it maps a sector in the time a cruiser crosses it.
A fast, variable-geometry explorer with bio-neural computers and the legs for very long missions. Lightly armored but hard to catch, it scouts and skirmishes with equal ease.
A wartime escort pairing an Intrepid-style saucer with a secondary hull. It was built quickly, in quantity, and it shows.
An Excelsior reworked into a gunship by trading its saucer lab space for weapons. Ugly, effective and cheap to field from older hulls.
A heavy torpedo cruiser with a launcher pod slung between twin hulls. It opens battles with a salvo few shields survive, then relies on escorts while it reloads.
A flat, broad-winged destroyer that presents a small target head-on. Designed for the Borg threat and pressed into service everywhere after.
A small, agile escort that fills the space between runabout and frigate. Cheap enough to lose, quick enough to outrun what it cannot kill.
A compact cruiser tuned for rapid response. It shares a design philosophy with the Akira but trades the torpedo pod for longer endurance.
An experimental tactical cruiser that splits into three independent attack vectors. Few designs can match its alpha strike, and none match its price tag.
A Nova hull rebuilt as a fighting frigate. It keeps the survey pedigree but gains the teeth to defend the systems it charts.
A fast courier ship used for dispatches in peacetime and for hit-and-run raids by anyone who can get one. Fragile but very quick.
A timeship from a distant future. Data only: it exists so a scenario or event can borrow it, never to be built in a campaign.
A late-era long-range explorer found in many community rosters. Included as reference data only; our numbers are our own.

roster.source: mod-derived: common in BOTF community rosters (Ultimate Universe, Galaxies at War, Vanilla+) and licensed games; not on screen before Discovery; exact mod stats vary and are not reproduced

ships.description: A mushroom-domed orbital shipyard large enough to swallow starships whole. Reference data for station art; campaign starbases use the station rules.

roster.source: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock

ships.description: A frontier trading post on a disputed border. Reference data for station art and event scenes.
The Empire's early battle cruiser, with a bulbous command pod and a lot of guns. Crude by later standards and entirely sincere about violence.
A small scout-escort that roams ahead of the fleet looking for trouble. When it finds some, it usually starts it.
The first Klingon ship to carry the bird-of-prey name: a raider with forward-heavy guns and little else. Honest, cheap, brutal.
The classic Klingon battle cruiser of the frontier years. A match for its Starfleet rivals and the ancestor of a century of warships.
An older bird-of-prey variant kept flying by houses that cannot afford better. It relies on its cloak to choose fights it can win.
A heavy cruiser name that turns up in community rosters. Reference data only; the stats are a remaster estimate.

ships.description: A fast, beetle-shaped attack ship crewed by soldiers bred for war. Its polaron beams cut through shields tuned for other weapons.
The Dominion's line capital, a heavy polaron platform that leads Jem'Hadar swarms into battle.
A vast late-war warship that outmasses anything the Alliance could field. Few were seen; one was usually enough.
A sleek, asymmetric warship whose energy-dampening weapon can leave a target adrift and powerless. The first shot matters most.
A smaller Collective vessel used for scouting and long-range assimilation. Still a match for most line cruisers.
A small Collective scout. When one is seen, something larger is rarely far behind.
An armored combat variant of the Borg cube. Reference data for encounters no empire should seek.
A command vessel for the heart of the Collective. Reference data only.
A tiny Collective craft that carries a handful of drones. Wrecks of this kind are how many first encounters begin.
A small crystalline ship that works in pairs or packs to spin an energy web around its prey. Punctual, territorial and patient.
A heavy, deliberate warship from a reptilian power that guards its borders fiercely. Tough rather than quick.
A fast raider built for piracy and smuggling. It runs from anything its own size and preys on everything smaller.
A lone hunter's ship with long legs and strong sensors. It tracks prey across sectors, then fights at a time of its choosing.
A large vessel for a whole hunting party. Heavy weapons, heavy armor and a crew that treats battle as sport.
A small fighter-raider flown by feuding sects. Individually weak, collectively a menace.
A huge, slow carrier-warship that is each sect's flagship and status symbol. Its guns are many and not very precise.
A warship of a people ravaged by disease, armed to take what they need to survive. Its boarding parties are feared more than its guns.
A tiny, agile craft that docks by the hundred into a single helix. Hard to hit, easy to underestimate.
An aggressive warship of the Xindi's most militant species. It hits hard and asks questions rarely.
A fast, compact warship that fights in close formation. Swarm tactics make up for thin armor.
An enormous, water-filled cruiser for a patient species. Slow to anger and slower to turn, but it shrugs off a great deal of fire.
A sturdy, practical ship of the Xindi's engineers and diplomats. Built to last rather than to dominate.
A planet-killing superweapon. Data only, for scenario and event use.
A living ship from fluidic space whose organic weapons overwhelm conventional shields. An encounter hazard, not a buildable design.
A ship that erases targets from history. Data only; its presence in a campaign would be an event.
A patrol warship of an imperium that measures its borders in time as well as space. Its chroniton torpedoes slip past ordinary shields.
A gigantic waste hauler leaking theta radiation. Nobody wants it near their worlds, including its crew.
A heavily armed ship of an exile people bent on reclaiming youth by any means. Isolytic weapons make it unwelcome everywhere.
Whatever the resistance could buy, steal or repair. Fast and expendable, it strikes and vanishes into the Badlands.
A unique predator warbird with a perfect cloak and a weapon of mass destruction in its hull. Data only.
A patrol warship that searches every vessel crossing its space for telepaths. Thorough, well armed and humorless.
A ring-hulled Andorian battle cruiser, proud and fast. Its crews are as quick to take offense as to take action.
A Vulcan combat cruiser with a ring warp drive. Reserved, precise and superior to anything its neighbors fly, as its crews will explain.
A long-range Vulcan survey ship that watches younger spacefaring peoples with polite interest.
A sturdy militia warship built after the Occupation to guard Bajoran space. Modest, but fiercely crewed.
A solar-sail vessel from Bajor's ancient age of exploration. Data only, a touch of history for events and the codex.
A raider flown by pirates who take cargo, hostages and the occasional starship. Quick, cheap and mean.
A small Talarian craft for border patrol and reconnaissance, usually flying ahead of heavier warships.
An alternate-timeline survey ship. Flagged Kelvin: reference data only, never in a prime campaign.
The alternate-timeline Enterprise, larger and heavier than its prime cousin. Reference data only.
A secret alternate-timeline warship built for a war that never came. Reference data only.
An alternate-timeline Klingon patrol ship. Reference data only.
A future mining ship turned into an instrument of revenge. Reference data only.

buildings.name: Advanced Replicators
buildings.description: Second-generation food synthesizers with a far larger pattern library, and meals people actually enjoy. Raises the system's food output by a percentage.

buildings.name: Basic Replicators
buildings.description: Industrial food synthesizers that turn raw organic stock into nourishing, if unexciting, meals. Raises the system's food output by a percentage.

buildings.name: Bunker Network
buildings.description: Fortified tunnels, weapons caches and trained militia that make every invasion a long, bloody slog. Strengthens ground defense.

buildings.name: Charge Collectors
buildings.description: Lightning rods the size of mountains, tapping the static that builds in the frozen air of arctic worlds. Raises the system's energy output.

buildings.name: Communications Grid
buildings.description: Dedicated subspace relays that keep a distant world in constant contact with its government. Fewer misunderstandings, fewer grievances.

buildings.name: Orbital Battery
buildings.description: Armed satellites ringing a system's inhabited worlds. They savage troop landings but are outranged by heavy warships.

buildings.name: Dilithium Refinery
buildings.description: Raw dilithium ore is useless to a warp core until it is refined and recrystallized. This plant does that work, and starship construction depends on it.

buildings.name: Phoenix Facility
buildings.description: An intelligence archive that records everything each operative learns in real time. When an agent falls, the mission does not fall with them.

buildings.name: Aquaculture Center
buildings.description: Floating sea farms that turn an ocean world's shallows into cultivated fishing grounds. Raises food output.

buildings.name: Private Farms
buildings.description: State support for family-run farms that trade some efficiency for pride and quality. Adds food and raises morale.

buildings.name: Theoretical Simulators
buildings.description: Computing halls where theorists test ideas against virtual universes before running a single real experiment. Raises the system's research output.

buildings.name: Subatomic Simulators
buildings.description: Particle laboratories fed by a dedicated warp reactor, able to recreate conditions found only inside stars. A large boost to the system's research output.

buildings.name: Subspace Scanner
buildings.description: A ground-based array that listens for the ripple a warp drive leaves in subspace. Extends sensor range.

buildings.name: Listening Post
buildings.description: A remote station whose analysts can pick a single warp signature out of a sector's background noise. Sees farther than a basic scanner.

buildings.name: Isolinear Scanner
buildings.description: Isolinear processing lets this array sift faint warp traces from much deeper space. Long sensor range without giving its position away.

buildings.name: Basic Shipyard
buildings.description: Orbital docks and construction slips where starships are assembled, overhauled and resupplied. Required to build ships, and a source of fleet supply.

buildings.name: Forced-labor Farms
buildings.description: Convict gangs work the fields under guard. The harvest improves; the public mood does not.

buildings.name: Trade Center
buildings.description: A bustling commodities exchange that draws merchants from neighboring systems. Raises the system's credit income.

buildings.name: Trade Goods
buildings.description: Instead of building projects, the system's factories turn out goods for market. Converts industry into credits.

buildings.name: Wind Turbines
buildings.description: Towering rotor farms planted where nothing else will grow, spinning in near-constant gales. Raises the system's energy output.

buildings.name: Shield Generator
buildings.description: Starship deflector technology scaled up to cover whole cities. It is not impenetrable, but it turns a massacre from orbit into a siege.

buildings.name: Union Shipyard
buildings.description: Cardassian construction slips run with military discipline. Builds and repairs the Union's ships and extends its fleet supply.

buildings.name: Re-education Center
buildings.description: Compulsory classes in loyalty for anyone who complains too loudly. Suppresses unrest, whatever its graduates privately think.

buildings.name: Obsidian Order
buildings.description: Cardassia's secret police, whose files hold something on everyone. Strengthens internal security; few citizens care to test it.

buildings.name: Covert Sensor Array
buildings.description: A military sensor net hidden inside what looks like harmless civilian astronomy. Long sensor range that enemies rarely think to target.

buildings.name: Central Command
buildings.description: The high command of the Cardassian military, and the school every officer must pass. New ships enter service with experienced crews.

buildings.name: Labor Camp
buildings.description: Guarded work compounds where the unemployed and the unwanted are made productive. Industry rises, at a cost in morale.

buildings.name: Inquisition
buildings.description: Door-to-door interrogations until someone names the ringleaders. Restores order to a troubled system.

buildings.name: Fantasy Land
buildings.description: A Ferengi holiday world of holosuites, casinos and spas, every one metered by the minute. Raises morale and pulls in tourist latinum.

buildings.name: Holo Cinema
buildings.description: Public holosuites where anyone can star in their own adventure for an evening. Raises morale.

buildings.name: Commerce Authority
buildings.description: The Alliance's regulatory arm audits every business, and its auditors report on more than accounts. Improves Ferengi espionage.

buildings.name: Tower of Commerce
buildings.description: The Alliance's trade licensing bureau, which takes its cut of every cargo that moves. Raises the income of every trade route.

buildings.name: Franchise Office
buildings.description: Where the Alliance registers its trademarks and bills the galaxy for using them. Generates credits.

buildings.name: Festival of Fun
buildings.description: A mandatory shopping holiday; nothing calms a restless Ferengi world like a sale. Quells unrest.

buildings.name: Genesis Research Lab
buildings.description: A Federation institute chasing the dream of making dead worlds live. Boosts Biotech research.

buildings.name: Daystrom Institute
buildings.description: Richard Daystrom's legacy: the Federation's leading computer science center, home of the duotronic revolution. Boosts Computers research.

buildings.name: Federation Council
buildings.description: The Federation's parliament, where every member world has a seat and a voice. Raises contentment across the Federation.

buildings.name: Starfleet Academy
buildings.description: The school in San Francisco where Starfleet officers are made. New ships enter service with experienced crews.

buildings.name: Utopia Planitia
buildings.description: The great orbital yards above Mars, birthplace of Starfleet's most famous ships. Speeds starship production.

buildings.name: Martial Law
buildings.description: Curfews, checkpoints and troops in the streets. A blunt last resort against unrest.

buildings.name: Hall of Warriors
buildings.description: A great hall hung with the banners of legendary warriors, where young Klingons swear to earn a place among them. Strengthens ground combat.

buildings.name: Mining Prison
buildings.description: A frozen penal colony where convicts dig dilithium until their sentences, or they, run out. Produces dilithium, and resentment with it.

buildings.name: Great Hall
buildings.description: Seat of the High Council on Qo'noS, where the Great Houses feud, bargain and swear loyalty. Raises contentment across the Empire.

buildings.name: Tactical College
buildings.description: Where Klingon officers study the battles of their ancestors, and of their enemies. New ships enter service with experienced crews.

buildings.name: Police State
buildings.description: The Council suspends custom and lets its enforcers settle matters personally. Quells unrest.

buildings.name: Combat Testing Center
buildings.description: A weapons range where new disruptors and torpedoes are fired until they break or prove themselves. Boosts Weapons research.

buildings.name: Singularity Plant
buildings.description: Romulan engineers bottle artificial black holes to power their warp cores. It frees the fleet from dilithium and works on any world.

buildings.name: Astrophysics Academy
buildings.description: Romulan astronomers catalogue every star and anomaly within reach, and some beyond it. Boosts Energy research.

buildings.name: Imperial Senate
buildings.description: The Senate chamber on Romulus, where the Empire's nobles debate and plot. Raises contentment across the Empire.

buildings.name: TalShiar Headquarters
buildings.description: The Empire's feared intelligence service, answerable to almost no one. Strengthens internal security.

buildings.name: Naval Academy
buildings.description: Romulan officer training, heavy on patience, deception and the cloak. New ships enter service with experienced crews.

buildings.name: Tribunal
buildings.description: Swift closed-door trials for anyone suspected of disloyalty. Quells unrest.

buildings.name: Alliance Shipyard
buildings.description: Ferengi docks where every bolt is invoiced. Builds and repairs Alliance ships and extends fleet supply.

buildings.name: Federation Replicator
buildings.description: Starfleet-standard food synthesizers installed across a colony's public spaces. Raises the system's food output by a percentage.

buildings.name: Starfleet Shipyard
buildings.description: A Starfleet yard where ships are built, refitted and sent back out. Required for construction and a source of fleet supply.

buildings.name: Military Shipyard
buildings.description: Klingon war docks where new ships are forged and battle damage is mended. Required for construction and a source of fleet supply.

buildings.name: Acamarian Clan Hall
buildings.description: Neutral ground where Acamarian clans settle disputes with words instead of blood. Raises credits and morale; requires Acamarian residents.

buildings.name: Andorian War College
buildings.description: Andorian officers teach the hard-won art of close combat. New ships gain experience; requires Andorian residents.

buildings.name: Super Soldier Academy
buildings.description: Angosian veterans pass on the conditioning that made them the most dangerous soldiers of their war. Strengthens ground combat; requires Angosian residents.

buildings.name: Mustering Base
buildings.description: An Antican recruiting depot that never lacks volunteers while the Selay live. Strengthens ground defense; requires Antican residents.

buildings.name: Harvesting Complex

buildings.name: Bajoran Jalanda Forum
buildings.description: A public amphitheater where vedeks and citizens debate the issues of the day. Guards against unrest; requires Bajoran residents.

buildings.name: Architectural Center

buildings.name: Industrial Center

buildings.name: Counseling Academy
buildings.description: Betazoid telepaths train counselors who can feel resentment long before it turns to sabotage. Strengthens internal security; requires Betazoid residents.

buildings.name: Cosmetology Center
buildings.description: Bolian beauty clinics with a discreet back room, where agents leave looking like someone else entirely. Improves espionage success; requires Bolian residents.

buildings.name: Planetary Computer

buildings.name: Research Think Tank

buildings.name: Gladiatorial Arena

buildings.name: Palace of Edo
buildings.description: Gardens, games and festivities open to every visitor who keeps the rules. Raises morale; requires Edo residents.

buildings.name: Ktarian Game Studio
buildings.description: Designers of entertainment so compelling that enemy crews stop working to play it. Improves sabotage; requires Ktarian residents.

buildings.name: Kinetics Laboratory
buildings.description: Malcorian warp-field theorists, freed from secrecy, test radical engine concepts. Boosts Propulsion research; requires Malcorian residents.

buildings.name: Mintakan Farm

buildings.name: Monument of Surrender

buildings.name: Recruitment Center

buildings.name: Collection Facility

buildings.name: Selay Mustering Base

buildings.name: Bioengineering Center

buildings.name: Physics Institute

buildings.name: Defense Network
buildings.description: Layered Talarian bunkers, minefields and gun pits built to make any landing a slaughter. Greatly strengthens ground defense; requires Talarian residents.

buildings.name: Mythology Library

buildings.name: Research Committee

buildings.name: Psychohistorical Archive

minorRaces.description: A clan society healing from centuries of blood feuds, with some clans still roaming the stars as raiders. Membership brings their trade networks and a steady flow of credits.
Proud, antennaed warriors from an icy moon and old partners of the Vulcans and humans. Their soldiers harden the ground defenses of every world in the empire they join.
A peaceful society that once engineered its soldiers into living weapons, then struggled to live with them. Their veterans stiffen the defenses of allied worlds.
Ichthyoid travelers who fall into a stupor aboard starships and rarely trust outsiders. Their ocean harvests add to the food supply of any empire they join.
Carnivorous hunters locked in an ancient feud with the neighboring Selay. Their appetite for battle strengthens the garrisons of any empire they join.
A deeply spiritual people who endured a brutal occupation with their faith intact. They despise Cardassian rule, and their devotion lifts morale across the empire they join.
Gracious hosts and gifted builders whose showpiece station charmed visitors until its secret came out. Their architects lift industry across any empire they join.
Methodical perfectionists who never solve the same problem twice. Their efficiency experts raise industry throughout the empire they join.
Telepaths who prize honesty because little can be hidden from them for long. Their counselors ease tension on every world of the empire they join.
Cheerful blue-skinned bankers whose financial houses reach across the quadrant. Membership opens their banks and raises credit income empire-wide.
Paired beings who think in binary and live linked to their planetary computer. Their network adds 10% to the research of any empire they join.
Tall, gentle scholars who value pure research far above commerce. Their think tanks add to the research of any empire they join.
Anarchist hunters who recognize no authority but strength. If persuaded to join an empire, they make its worlds very costly to invade.
A carefree, pleasure-loving people watched over by a powerful guardian entity. Their easygoing culture raises morale across the empire they join.
Ambitious schemers who once tried to subvert a starship crew with an addictive game. Wary of outsiders, they drive a hard bargain but put industrious hands to work.
A people on the verge of warp flight who are not yet ready to learn they are not alone. Suspicious of every empire, they bring a busy industrial base to one that wins them over.
A gentle, rational proto-Vulcan people who once briefly mistook a starship captain for a god. Their communal farms add to the food supply of any empire they join.
Pacifists who have outlasted repeated conquests by never resisting any of them. Their calm steadies morale in the empire they join.
Towering brawlers and hired muscle with a taste for violence. Their young warriors swell the garrisons of any empire that can hold their loyalty.
Slow-spoken scavengers who acquire technology by trade, trickery or theft. What they collect adds a little to the research of any empire they join.
Reptilian rivals of the Anticans, just as eager to settle old scores. Their soldiers strengthen the garrisons of any empire they join.
Legalistic non-humanoids who consider most species barely worth addressing and enforce every clause of every treaty. Their mastery of environments boosts food output empire-wide.
A people whose decentralized bodies shrug off wounds that would kill others. Their curiosity about physical forces adds to the research of any empire they join.
A patriarchal military society that treasures its homeworld above all else. Their fortification doctrine makes every world of their empire harder to invade.
The Children of Tama speak only in metaphors drawn from their myths and history. Once understood, those stories hold insights that raise the research of any empire they join.
Humanoids who share their lives with long-lived symbionts that carry centuries of memory from host to host. Their joined scientists raise the research of any empire they join.
Telepathic historians who collect the memories of other peoples as living archives. Their knowledge adds a little to the research of any empire they join.
Disciples of logic with a scientific tradition older than their warp drive. Vulcan scholars add 15% to the research of any empire they join.
Information dealers who will sell any secret to anyone who can pay. Their brokerage houses raise credit income for any empire they join.
Celebrated as the finest strategic minds in the galaxy, though they rarely put the reputation to the test. Their war-planners strengthen the defenses of any empire they join.
